config.title: Grid template areas

intro.title: Grid template areas
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage layout using CSS Grid template areas to arrange content into distinct sections like header, main content, sidebar, and footer. You will learn how to define named grid areas in your CSS and assign them to HTML elements to create a clean, structured design without complex positioning code. The main technologies involved are CSS Grid and the grid-template-areas property, which allows you to visually map out your layout. By the end, you'll be able to create responsive, organized page layouts quickly and intuitively.
intro.usecase: Grid template areas are essential for creating complex, responsive layouts in modern web applications. You'll use this technique to build dashboard interfaces where you need to position multiple panels (charts, tables, metrics) in specific arrangements that adapt to different screen sizes. Content management systems often employ grid areas to organize article layouts with headers, sidebars, main content, and footers. News websites and e-commerce product pages use this approach to create visually structured content grids that maintain consistent spacing and alignment across devices.

objectives: Construct a CSS grid layout using named template areas
Configure grid container properties to define area placement
Apply grid-area declarations to assign child elements to specific regions
Manipulate grid template areas to rearrange layout structures
Integrate grid template areas with other CSS grid properties
Implement responsive designs by modifying template areas with media queries
Control element positioning within grid areas using alignment properties

steps.title: Create a container element with display: grid
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a class named '.container' that sets display to grid.
steps.hint: Use the .container selector followed by curly braces, then add the display property with the value grid.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule for .container that enables grid layout.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added 'display: grid;' inside the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Create a CSS rule for .container with display: grid.

steps.title: Define grid template columns and rows
steps.instruction: Add the grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows properties to the .container selector to create a 3-column, 2-row grid structure.
steps.hint: Use grid-template-columns to define three equal-width columns and grid-template-rows to define two equal-height rows. You can use the repeat() function for equal sizing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container selector will have both grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows properties defined with appropriate values.
successCriteria: grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows properties are added to the .container selector with valid CSS values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added both grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows properties to the .container selector.

steps.title: Introduce grid-template-areas property
steps.instruction: Add a grid-template-areas property to the .container selector with named area layout that matches your grid structure.
steps.hint: The grid-template-areas property uses quoted strings to define named areas in your grid. Each string represents a row, and each word in the string represents a column.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container selector now has a grid-template-areas property defining named areas for your grid layout.
successCriteria: The grid-template-areas property is added to the .container selector with valid syntax (quoted strings for rows).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check the syntax. The grid-template-areas property should use quoted strings, with each string representing a row and each word representing a column area.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid-template-areas property wasn't added correctly. Make sure you add it inside the .container selector with the proper syntax.

steps.title: Create child elements for the grid
steps.instruction: Add three div elements inside the container with class names 'header', 'sidebar', and 'content'.
steps.hint: Create three separate div elements, each with a different class name that matches the areas you'll define later.
steps.expectedOutcome: Three div elements with class names 'header', 'sidebar', and 'content' are added as children of the container.
successCriteria: The CSS contains three div elements with the class names 'header', 'sidebar', and 'content'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly three div elements with the correct class names.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please add three div elements with class names 'header', 'sidebar', and 'content'.

steps.title: Assign grid-area property to first child
steps.instruction: Add a grid-area property to the first child element (the first div) and set its value to 'header'.
steps.hint: The grid-area property places an element in a named grid area. Use the area name you defined in grid-template-areas.
steps.expectedOutcome: The first child element will be assigned to the 'header' grid area.
successCriteria: The first child element has a grid-area property with the value 'header'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the grid-area property to the first child element with the correct value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The first child element doesn't have the grid-area property set to 'header'. Check your CSS selector and property value.

steps.title: Assign grid-area property to second child
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the second child element (div:nth-child(2)) and assign it a grid-area property with a different area name than the first child.
steps.hint: Use the selector div:nth-child(2) and set grid-area to a named area you plan to define in grid-template-areas.
steps.expectedOutcome: The second child element will be positioned in a different named grid area when grid-template-areas is defined.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for div:nth-child(2) is added with a grid-area property set to a named area.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a rule for the second child, but make sure it includes the grid-area property with a named area value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The second child element rule is missing or doesn't have the grid-area property. Try adding div:nth-child(2) { grid-area: yourAreaName; }.

steps.title: Assign grid-area property to third child
steps.instruction: Add a grid-area property to the third child element using another area name from your grid-template-areas definition.
steps.hint: Use the grid-area property with the area name you defined for the third position in your grid-template-areas.
steps.expectedOutcome: The third child element will be positioned in the grid according to the area name you assign.
successCriteria: The third child element has a grid-area property with a valid area name.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using a valid area name from your grid-template-areas.
steps.feedbackWrong: The third child element doesn't have a grid-area property yet. Try adding one with an area name.

steps.title: Create overlapping grid areas
steps.instruction: Modify the grid-template-areas property in the .container rule to create overlapping regions by repeating area names across multiple cells.
steps.hint: In the grid-template-areas value, you can make areas overlap by having the same area name appear in multiple positions. For example, 'header header header' would make the header area span three columns.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid-template-areas property will be updated to create overlapping regions by repeating area names in the grid definition.
successCriteria: The grid-template-areas property contains repeated area names to create overlapping regions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the grid-template-areas property needs to have repeated area names to create actual overlapping regions. Try making some areas span multiple cells.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid-template-areas property doesn't show overlapping regions. Remember to repeat area names in the grid definition to make areas span multiple cells.

steps.title: Add visual styling to distinguish areas
steps.instruction: Add background colors and padding to the first three child elements to make the grid areas visually distinct.
steps.hint: Use the background-color property with different colors for each selector, and add some padding inside each element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The first three grid areas will have different background colors and padding, making them easier to distinguish in the layout.
successCriteria: The first three child element selectors each have a background-color property and a padding property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure all three child elements have both background-color and padding properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The styling properties weren't added correctly. Check that you're adding background-color and padding to the existing child selectors.

steps.title: Adjust grid gap for spacing
steps.instruction: Add a grid-gap or gap property to the .container rule to create spacing between the grid areas.
steps.hint: Use either 'grid-gap' (older) or 'gap' (modern shorthand) with a value like 10px or 1rem.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid items will have visible spacing between them, making the layout clearer and more visually separated.
successCriteria: The .container rule includes a grid-gap or gap property with a valid CSS length value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the spacing property might be missing or incomplete. Make sure to add grid-gap or gap with a value like 10px.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid spacing hasn't been added correctly. Check that you've added grid-gap or gap inside the .container rule with a valid CSS length.
